parsed.explanation: Combined federal-state regime imposes universal birth-sex exposure: federal passports only M/F, facility bans, visa flagging for document doubt, and state bathroom bans in 21 states with trespass criminalisation in 4 and one documented 24-hour men's-ward detention. Courts enjoin some orders and 33 states plus DC lack mapped bans, and imprisonment or execution for trans presence is not documented. Custody-abuse claims are single-source and uncorroborated, discounted. Protective states and functioning courts mitigate but do not cancel enforced federal/state restrictions.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary passport rule, X eliminated for new issues, passports reported confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded; visa cable flags document doubt and directs refusal or fraud consideration.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud lifetime bar requires four elements, never automatic, limited waivers; passport policy under court challenge.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can trigger visa refusal and potential fraud inquiry, linking federal entry screening to state document invalidation risk.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One documented bathroom trespass arrest, handcuffed, held 24h in men's ward, up to 60 days possible; uncorroborated single-source claims of immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse and 2026 prison conversion-type policies.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented permanent fraud bar imposed for gender discrepancy; courts blocked/enjoined several executive orders; pretrial release obtained in documented arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest for facility use leads to birth-sex custody placement, the operative harm, even where charge is misdemeanour trespass.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal ban on government-funded single-sex facilities by gender identity; 21 states ban some or all government buildings/schools, 6 extend to some private settings, 4 criminalise after refusal to depart.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 other units and DC have no mapped ban, though other state sex-definition laws may affect access; statute has exemptions and requires willful entry plus refusal.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal rule applies in all states, state bans add criminal exposure in subset; traveller must plan itinerary by state and cannot avoid federal facilities.

care_services.exposure: 28 Jan 2025 order targets minor gender-affirming care; children's care banned in 27 states; proposed national insurance bar for under-18s; prison policies reportedly remove hormones.
care_services.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; proposed October 2025 health rule not final; adult routine care restrictions not documented.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor may face care denial and record scrutiny; adult with minor faces school/facility and investigation climate, but short-stay visitor care access is not shown as universally barred.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official binary definition, removal of gender-identity materials, sports ban, directing investigation/prosecution over school social transition, counterterrorism language including radically pro-transgender groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2020 Supreme Court employment ruling and national hate-crime statute remain; courts are actively reviewing orders; no reward posting documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing by federal institutions raises outing and enforcement probability, while litigation and injunctions create interstate and temporal inconsistency.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans-athlete entry ban, K-12 facility bans in 21 states, school investigation/prosecution order for facilitating social transition, minor care bans; guardians may lose facility/care access for minor.
minors_guardians.protection: Several minor-related orders blocked/enjoined; 33 states plus DC lack mapped facility bans; no documented visitor-parent prosecution.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor traveller adds school, sports, care and facility exposure; guardian's own document/facility mismatch compounds itinerary restriction.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific killing/violence rate documented; one bathroom arrest shows police enforcement; public support for birth-sex documents 66% and for sports alignment 69% signals hostile climate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; 22 states plus DC outlaw gender-identity discrimination; police/courts generally functioning, though 37 states lacked state bias statutes as of 2019.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Hostile public climate plus hostile facility law increases police-call and confrontation risk; functioning courts provide recourse after, not prevention during, encounter.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit unresolved after Supreme Court allowed restrictions to take effect; remedies vary by state; airport scanner trans-specific treatment not documented; do-not-travel list is one advocacy assessment.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, injunctions against several orders, legal-aid FAQ, and protective-state laws are operative mitigations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are real but slow and uneven; they reduce severity for some claims without restoring X passports or facility access in ban states.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal exclusion and no effective remedy for refused travellers, but here exclusion is by document/facility rather than routine border turn-away and courts do enjoin some measures, so slightly higher than 0.35.

Similar durable exposure via registration/documents and administrative holds without credible imprisonment or execution; here federal passport and criminal trespass in 4 states make exposure more coercive, pointing slightly below 0.45.

0.55 has ward placement by document with patient-advocate remedies and no detention pathway; here birth-sex facilities/custody plus visa fraud flagging and one arrest are more severe, so materially lower.
0.65 has brief detention ended by advocacy, apology/compensation and reliable court release; here intentional federal/state bans, stranded passports and no documented compensation make outcome worse.

parsed.synthesis: Operative regime combines nationwide birth-sex documents and federal facility exclusion with sharply varying state bans, including criminal trespass in four states. That universal exposure, one documented arrest with men's-ward detention, and visa flagging for doubt drive the rating down. Functioning courts, injunctions, many non-ban states, existing X validity and no documented execution or routine imprisonment keep it above severe-targeting tiers. Uncorroborated custody-abuse claims and unresolved litigation are treated as uncertain, not as safety.
